source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9

coverage.scope: F.2 assumption-then-assignment, §365(f)(2) assignee assurance, §365(k) release, anti-assignment clause overriding, subleases vs assignments, nonshopping-center Martin Paint full case and special shopping-center restrictions, Problem8.9 unanswered

topics.title: F.2(a–c) Assignment: Assume First, Release Estate, Antiassignment Override
topics.description: Sale of valuable executory contract and new obligor's performance promise.

entries.title: Assume BEFORE assign and cure defaults §365(f)(2)(A), §365(b)
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Trustee can transfer valuable contract only after formal assumption, paying/correcting existing defaults and actual pecuniary losses; assignee offers adequate assurance of future performance §365(f)(2)(B).
entries.laymanExplanation: Can't flip an under-market retail lease to a new shop without bringing landlord current and proving assignee capable.
entries.legalExplanation: Cure protects counterparty against prebankruptcy arrears, which may otherwise be ordinary unsecured.
entries.examApplication: Set order: existence → §365(c) restriction → assumption/cure → assignee assurance → assignment approval.
entries.examTrap: Do not say §365(f)(1) allows transferring any dead/nonassumable agreement.

entries.title: §365(k): estate relieved of postassignment breach
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: After assignment in bankruptcy trustee/estate has no liability for assignee's later performance breach, unlike common-law assignor responsibility; debtor's personal liability also affected by discharge.
entries.laymanExplanation: Old tenant sells cheap lease and is not guarantor of new tenant's later default under §365(k).
entries.legalExplanation: For that substitution nondebtor entitled meaningful evidence assignee will pay.
entries.examApplication: Compare with sublease where estate still owes rent.
entries.examTrap: Not automatic release merely because debtor sublets part of space.

entries.title: Antiassignment clauses usually unenforceable §365(f)(1)
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Ordinary contractual restrictions prohibiting, restricting or conditioning assignment are overridden, even if in applicable law generally enforcing such clauses, subject narrow §365(c) identity-based nondelegation.
entries.laymanExplanation: Contract says 'landlord may veto any assignment'—usually not enough to stop valuable bankruptcy assignment.
entries.legalExplanation: Special personal-service/genuine nondelegability and shopping-center assurances may constrain.
entries.examApplication: For Problem8.9 consider how 75% profit-sharing condition restricts assignment; leave result unanswered.
entries.examTrap: Do not assume all statutory/identity-specific bars to assignment erased.

entries.title: Financial value of discounted lease can be sold
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Example casebook: $8k/year remaining lease, market rent $13k/year, 1 year left => gross below-market contract spread $5k, before cure/transaction costs.
entries.laymanExplanation: Estate can sell opportunity to rent cheaply instead of let old landlord reclaim market spread.
entries.legalExplanation: Source distinguishes benefit captured for all creditors vs private lessor windfall.
entries.examApplication: Set up (market rent−contract rent)×remaining term, adjusted to cashflow and costs.
entries.examTrap: A negotiated assignment sale price may differ from theoretical spread.

entries.title: Sublease versus assignment: duties and clauses differ
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Assignment under §365(k) releases estate on future breaches, assignee independently assures performance, §365(f)(1) limits anti-assignment provisions. Sublease: estate remains liable to landlord, sublessee no (f)(2)(B) statutory assurance, anti-subletting clauses not overridden by (f)(1).
entries.laymanExplanation: Letting someone rent your unit while you remain responsible isn't same as handing over the lease entirely.
entries.legalExplanation: These distinctions impact monetizing lease and third-party risk.
entries.examApplication: Identify assignment or sublease based on actual transaction terms.

topics.title: F.2(d–e) Adequate Assurance and Shopping Center vs Nonshopping-Center
topics.description: Assignee's risk and special landlord/other-tenant protections.

entries.title: §365(f)(2)(B) adequate assurance mandatory for EVERY assignment
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Even if debtor had no prepetition default, forced assignment requires assurance assignee will perform in future, typically financial statements, working capital, reserve, business projections, guarantees, prior performance.
entries.laymanExplanation: Original landlord shouldn't be forced to trade a reliable tenant for insolvent stranger.
entries.legalExplanation: Assumption only demands assurance under §365(b)(1)(C) when defaulted; assignment ALWAYS.
entries.examApplication: Separate proof of assignee finances from cure of old defaults.
entries.examTrap: An antiassignment waiver doesn't waive assurance.

entries.title: Bankruptcy court assesses real practical performance risk
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Legislative history expects full economic benefit of nondebtor's bargain; judges require evidence assignee won't create greater default risk than original tenant.
entries.laymanExplanation: Business plan with projected positive receipts is weaker than actual available cash and reliable guarantees.
entries.legalExplanation: Review operating history, market demand, tenant suitability, rent security.
entries.examApplication: List concrete documents and explain risk.
entries.examTrap: Assignee merely saying 'I'll pay' is inadequate.

entries.title: §365(l) lessor may require usual security deposit
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Lessor under assigned lease can obtain deposit/other security substantially same as voluntary lease to comparable tenant.
entries.laymanExplanation: Landlord can request ordinary market-standard deposit when court substitutes new company.
entries.legalExplanation: Distinct from right to outright veto bankruptcy assignment.
entries.examApplication: Compare requested security to peer similar tenant.
entries.examTrap: Not unlimited extra deposit to defeat §365(f).

entries.title: Non-shopping-center may relax use clause upon actual/substantial detriment showing
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Without statutory §365(b)(3) shopping-center rule, court has discretion to approve deviation from nonshopping lease use restrictions unless landlord shows ACTUAL AND SUBSTANTIAL prejudice, not speculative competitive disadvantage.
entries.laymanExplanation: Paint store lease can go to apparel seller if landlord cannot prove real economic injury.
entries.legalExplanation: Source Martin Paint follows U.L. Radio reasoning and weighs landlord's financial expectations.
entries.examApplication: First determine whether location qualifies as shopping center.
entries.examTrap: Don't apply Martin Paint flexibility to special §365(b)(3) shopping-center leases.

entries.title: Shopping-center §365(b)(3) strict terms and tenant mix
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Mall/shopping center requires adequate assurance of source of rent, similar financial condition of assignee to original tenant, no substantial decline percentage rent, full compliance radius/location/use/exclusivity terms in its and related agreements, and no disruption of tenant mix.
entries.laymanExplanation: Mall built around coordinated anchor shops has stricter protections than stand-alone commercial building.
entries.legalExplanation: 1984 amendments removed 'substantially' from compliance with use/exclusivity and tenant mix, tipping balance toward lessors.
entries.examApplication: In 8.8 note shopping center cannot simply rebrand into takeout violating snowmobile-only use.
entries.examTrap: Don't call every multi-tenant block automatically nonshopping; Joshua Slocum counted streetfront case as center.

entries.title: What counts as shopping center: functional planned integration
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Code leaves undefined; legislative history discusses planned integrated development, master agreements, rental percentages, common amenities, tenant-mix planning; Joshua Slocum even found downtown block with one landlord may qualify.
entries.laymanExplanation: A row of small shops can be a shopping center on facts despite no big mall parking lot.
entries.examApplication: List unit planning and use coordination, not merely number of floors.
entries.examTrap: A building being 'commercial' does not necessarily make it statutory shopping center.

entries.title: Shopping-center limits apply on assumption of default AND assignment
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Assumption of defaulted shopping-center lease requires §365(b)(1)(C) future assurance; assignment always requires §365(f)(2)(B), each incorporates §365(b)(3) stringent criteria.
entries.laymanExplanation: Even staying as tenant can require assurances about required store use when in default.
entries.legalExplanation: Compare cure/going dark and new assignee proposal separately.
entries.examApplication: State triggering provision when applying shopping-center constraints.
entries.examTrap: Landlord's protections are not only for assignment cases.

topics.title: F.2(d) In re Martin Paint Stores (1996) — Full Case Brief
topics.description: Nonshopping-center paint store assignment to competing apparel seller, standing and legal impossibility.

entries.title: In re Martin Paint Stores, 199 B.R. 258 (Bankr. S.D.N.Y. 1996)
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Yes. Court overruled landlord Feldco and Persuasion objections and approved assignment: no actual and substantial harm to landlord shown, competing tenant lacked direct standing to challenge debtor lease, and court-approved assignment legally excused landlord from incompatible exclusivity promise under impossibility doctrine.
entries.laymanExplanation: For nonshopping-center lease, use clause deviation may be permitted absent proof actual/substantial landlord detriment; competing tenant doesn't automatically have standing to veto and possible conflicts with its lease may be excused through court-order impossibility on source facts.
entries.legalExplanation: For nonshopping-center leases, §365 policy favors capturing asset value; strict enforcement of use clause demands proof actual/substantial detriment, not speculative concern. Persuasion wasn't debtor creditor or beneficiary of Martin lease and lacked standing; court considered evidence anyway. Feldco fixed rent from rival regardless sales, many competitors nearby and new shop could bring customers, speculative 20% drop not enough. Court said judicial order rendered landlord's literal performance under separate exclusivity clause legally impossible without own fault, and avoided liability under state contract impossibility; otherwise other tenants could veto valuable estate assignments contrary §365(f). Shopping center §365(b)(3) explicitly different.
entries.examApplication: Mention $75k bid, $18k cure, $40k estate gain, $9.5k rent, fixed competitor rent, existing neighborhood clothing competitors, asserted 20% dip, tenant standing.
entries.examTrap: Not general authorization to breach ANY unrelated third-party lease without consequence; §365(b)(3) shopping centers enforce strict exclusivity, and impossibility rationale is contested in chapter questions.
entries.sourceRole: Full judicial opinion excerpted in supplied Chapter8
entries.facts: Paint/hardware retailer Martin Paint Chapter11 filed Aug18 1995 with ~30 stores, failed reorganization and auctioned leases. Pretty Girl clothing company bid $75k for Bronx 947 Southern Blvd storefront lease at $9,500/month through July2007, with $18k arrears to Feldco landlord and estimated ~$40k net benefit after cure/commissions. Lease limited paint/hardware/home improvement. Other building tenant Persuasion Ladies' Stores had a lease barring landlord from leasing in same building to store selling ladies' clothes EXCLUSIVELY; Persuasion/landlord objected. Feldco admitted building not a shopping center. Rival already faced neighborhood competitors; rival's rent fixed not percent-of-sales; financial ability of Pretty Girl not disputed.
entries.issue: Can Chapter11 estate assume and assign NONshopping-center store lease from paint retailer to women's apparel company despite use clause and another tenant's exclusivity, when landowner claims lost rent/competition?
entries.holding: Yes. Court overruled landlord Feldco and Persuasion objections and approved assignment: no actual and substantial harm to landlord shown, competing tenant lacked direct standing to challenge debtor lease, and court-approved assignment legally excused landlord from incompatible exclusivity promise under impossibility doctrine.
entries.reasoning: For nonshopping-center leases, §365 policy favors capturing asset value; strict enforcement of use clause demands proof actual/substantial detriment, not speculative concern. Persuasion wasn't debtor creditor or beneficiary of Martin lease and lacked standing; court considered evidence anyway. Feldco fixed rent from rival regardless sales, many competitors nearby and new shop could bring customers, speculative 20% drop not enough. Court said judicial order rendered landlord's literal performance under separate exclusivity clause legally impossible without own fault, and avoided liability under state contract impossibility; otherwise other tenants could veto valuable estate assignments contrary §365(f). Shopping center §365(b)(3) explicitly different.
entries.rule: For nonshopping-center lease, use clause deviation may be permitted absent proof actual/substantial landlord detriment; competing tenant doesn't automatically have standing to veto and possible conflicts with its lease may be excused through court-order impossibility on source facts.

entries.title: Why rival Persuasion lacked standing
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Persuasion wasn't debtor creditor, debtor's lease party or intended beneficiary of Martin Paint use clause, so not entitled to demand §365 assurance, which belongs landlord; court considered equivalent evidence in landlord's own objection.
entries.laymanExplanation: Neighbor store can't independently veto just because it dislikes competition.
entries.legalExplanation: Court separates economic competitive concerns from statutory standing to object.
entries.examApplication: Who may invoke rights under particular lease?
entries.examTrap: A rival tenant can have its own contract claim against landlord; standing issue isn't necessarily substantive extinguishment.

entries.title: Actual and substantial detriment was NOT shown
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Persuasion's lease rent was fixed and no evidence Pretty Girl entry threatened collection; clothing competition already existed; landlord's worry about rival sales and percentage-rent nonexistent.
entries.laymanExplanation: More competition isn't automatically proof landlord will lose rent.
entries.legalExplanation: Protects estate's ~$40k surplus subject payment of arrears and assignee performance.
entries.examApplication: Use evidence and actual landlord exposure.
entries.examTrap: Not a blanket rule that tenant-mix concerns never matter.

entries.title: Impossibility defense for landlord's other exclusivity covenant
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
entries.summary: Court reasoned involuntary judicially approved assignment makes fulfillment of separate exclusivity promise legally impossible, without landlord causal fault, preventing landlord damages for unavoidable breach.
entries.laymanExplanation: Judge compelled new tenant, landlord didn't choose to violate rival's covenant.
entries.legalExplanation: Book calls a potentially sweeping Catch-22; shouldn't mechanically extrapolate.
entries.examApplication: Explain interplay of §365(f) and nondebtor third-party agreements.
entries.examTrap: This is lower-court holding under specific state-law impossibility reasoning.

topics.description: Lease value allocation and indirect contractual conditions.

problems.title: Problem 8.9 — 75% assignment premium
problems.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy Chapter8 §F.2 assignment, full In re Martin Paint Stores opinion, §§365(f),(k),(l),(b)(3), original Problem8.9
problems.prompt: Debtor tenant leases retail space for $20,000 annual rent. Clause requires tenant pay lessor 75% of all assignee amounts exceeding base rental as CONDITION of assignment. Debtor Chapter11 seeks assume and assign to assignee for $28,000/year. Lessor objects demanding $6,000, representing 75% of $8,000 yearly spread. Analyze §§365(f)(1),(f)(2), cure and anti-assignment restrictions, without solving original.
